lesson.subject: inquiry
lesson.title: Think Like a Shark
lesson.subtitle: Shark Tank | Term 4 Week 3, Session 2
lesson.footer: Shark Tank | Year 5/6 Inquiry | Week 3 Session 2

plan.curriculum: Victorian Curriculum Economics and Business, Levels 5 and 6: why businesses exist and how people make choices about where their money goes; Design and Technologies, Levels 5 and 6: evaluating design ideas against criteria
plan.shape: watch, model, judge: a young entrepreneur the sharks loved but did not invest in, buying versus investing, the four-check shark checklist, a judging round, then 30 minutes of team forming and shortlisting with Grade 6 consultants
plan.criticalFeature: a shark invests in a business that can grow, not in one product to take home; the four checks are the same ones the Grade 6s use on Shark Tank Day
decisionPoints: the choice check: what did the shark do with the tokens
the exit board: judge a new pitch with one check
plan.anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Say: every product starts with a problem, and upcycling makes the fix from something already made. Seat them with a team that has a Junk Lab sketch.

studentTools: Session 1 Worksheets and Junk Lab sketches
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Write the four shark checks on the board: Real problem? Upcycled? Can they make it work? Will people want it?
Grade 5 business teams of three or four, written up before the session. Group by shared ideas, not friendships
Each Grade 5 team gets two or three Grade 6s as its consultant sharks
videos: Luv Ur Self on Shark Tank Australia: Isabella Dymalovski, aged 13 (youtube.com/watch?v=aDS5mmZij-4)

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Buying or investing, the shark checklist, then your team's shortlist of three ideas.
resources.title: Idea Shortlist
resources.subtitle: Sharks invest. They don't buy.

example.prompt: Mum pays $3 for a cupcake at the school fete. Buying or investing?
steps: She gets one cupcake to keep.
Money for one product is buying.

items.prompt: Sort each one: buying or investing?
cards: gives money so a team makes more
gets a share of the earnings
takes home a jar of slime

buying: takes home a jar of slime
investing: gives money so a team makes more
gets a share of the earnings

example.prompt: Pot plant holders made from old tins, because plants keep falling off the windowsill.
steps: Real problem? Yes. Upcycled? Yes, old tins.
Can they make it work? Yes. Will people want it? Yes.
example.answer: Invest: it passes all four checks.

items.prompt: Write yes or no for each check.
rows: Ball bags sewn from old pillowcases, because balls roll away
A new plastic toy car, because toy cars are fun
A cardboard robot that tidies your room
answers: Ball bags sewn from old pillowcases, because balls roll away
A new plastic toy car, because toy cars are fun
A cardboard robot that tidies your room

items.prompt: Which idea would you invest in? Circle it.
items.explain: The ball bags. They pass all four checks; the car is not upcycled and fixes no problem, and the robot cannot really be made.

example.prompt: Shortlist one idea: a cord tidy from toilet roll tubes.
steps: Name the problem: cords tangle behind the TV.
Count the checks it passes: 4 out of 4.
example.answer: Cord Keeper | tangled cords | 4 out of 4

items.prompt: Write your team's three best ideas.
answers: e.g. Hat clips from bread tags
e.g. A drink bottle sling from an old belt

items.prompt: Jack explains investing. Find his mistake and fix it.
work: Investing means buying lots of the product.
So a shark takes home ten of them.
items.answer: Investing is not buying. The shark gives money to help the business grow and gets a share of what it earns, not the products.

items.prompt: Which idea is your team's favourite so far? Give a reason from the checklist.
items.answer: e.g. Hat clips, because they pass all four checks and every kid at school loses a hat.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: work out what a shark gets back for investing.
resources.title: Extension: The Shark's Share
resources.subtitle: Sharks invest for a share of what the business earns.

sections.title: Work out the shark's share
sections.intro: When a shark owns half of a business, the shark gets half of what it earns. A quarter of the business means a quarter of the earnings.

example.prompt: A shark owns half of a cupcake business. The business earns $40. How much does the shark get?

items.prompt: A shark owns a quarter of a bird bath business. The business earns $80. How much does the shark get?
A shark owns half of a candle business. The shark got $35. How much did the business earn?

example.prompt: Shark A gives $100 for half the business. Shark B gives $100 for a quarter. Which deal is better for the team?
steps: Shark B wants a smaller share.
The team keeps more with Shark B.
example.answer: Shark B's deal: the team keeps three quarters.

items.prompt: Three sharks each offer a team $60. Which deal lets the team keep the most?
items.explain: $60 for a quarter. The team gives away the smallest share, so it keeps three quarters of the earnings.

resources.label: Grade 6 Consultant Card
resources.description: For each Grade 6 consultant shark: the four questions to ask their team.
resources.title: Consultant Shark Card
resources.subtitle: You are a shark. Ask, don't build.

blocks.heading: Ask your team these four questions

checklist: What problem does it fix, and who has that problem?
What is it made from? Was it something old?
Can your team build it from junk in two build sessions?
Who would want it? How do you know?

blocks.heading: One tip I gave my team

blocks.tip: Remember: on Shark Tank Day you invest your tokens. You don't buy.

slides.notes: Session 2 of Shark Tank. One line: today we learn to think like a shark, and the Grade 5s form their business teams.

Teams written up before the session from the Session 1 Worksheets; two or three Grade 6s matched to each team. Cue the Luv Ur Self clip. Print the Worksheet one per Grade 5, a few Extension and Supported copies, and one Consultant Card per Grade 6.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning what makes a business worth investing in.
successCriteria: I can explain the difference between buying and investing.
I can judge an idea with the four shark checks.
I can use the shark checks to choose my team's best ideas.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Last week we found problems. Today we think like the sharks who judge them.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Grade 6s, you're the sharks on the day, so this is your training.
Grade 5s, today you meet your business team.
notes.prep: SC1 buying versus investing is reachable for all; SC2 the four checks is the core; SC3 is the team shortlist. Anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.

visual.label: Watch on YouTube: Luv Ur Self

notes.answer: open - the sharks loved her, but none invested
beats: PLAY 0:00 to 3:00, the pitch. The player stops itself; the full clip is 10:31.
SAY: Isabella was 13. Watch her pitch like a shark would.
ASK: Would you invest in Isabella's business?
10 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mostly thumbs up
SAY: Here's what happened. The sharks loved her, but none invested.
They all offered to help her instead.
ASK: Why might a shark say no to someone they like?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: they worried about the business, school, time
trap: thinking a likeable pitcher always gets a deal.
Fix: sharks judge the business, not the person. Student restates.
notes.prep: Launch. Sharks judge whether the business can grow. The sharks worried she could not balance school and a business; Andrew Banks later helped her into stores.
notes.sources: Luv Ur Self, Shark Tank Australia; SmartCompany recap of Isabella Dymalovski's pitch.

slides.meaning: To give money to a business so it can grow, in return for a share of what it earns.
slides.example: The sharks didn't buy Carson's board. They invested in his business.

notes.answer: giving money so a business can grow, for a share of what it earns
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Invest. Say it with me. In-vest.
SAY: When you invest, you don't take a product home.
You help the business grow, and you get a share of what it earns.
ASK: Does a shark who invests take the product home?
10 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: no
trap: thinking investing means buying lots of the product.
Fix: ask what the shark gets back, student says a share of the earnings.
notes.prep: The key word for the Grade 6s. On Shark Tank Day they invest tokens; they never buy.

rows: Money to help the business grow
A share of what it earns

notes.answer: investing: the shark helps the business grow and shares what it earns
beats: POINT to the Buying column.
SAY: When I buy a Pocket Pal, I hand over money and take one home. Done.
POINT to the Investing column.
SAY: When I invest, I help the Pocket Pal team make more.
If the business does well, I get a share.
ASK: Grade 6s give tokens on Shark Tank Day. Buying or investing?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: investing
trap: Grade 6s choosing the product they want to own.
Fix: ask which business you'd help grow, student re-chooses.
notes.stretch: Why would a shark invest in a business they don't personally need?
notes.help: Cover the right column; ask what you get when you buy.
notes.prep: The model for SC1. Pocket Pal is the class model business; say it the same way every time.

slides.title: The four shark checks
slides.label: The same four checks the sharks use on Shark Tank Day

notes.answer: yes to all four for Pocket Pal
beats: POINT to each check in turn.
SAY: Real problem? Upcycled? Can they make it work? Will people want it?
SAY: Let me check Pocket Pal. Hats fall off hooks, so yes, a real problem.
Old jeans, so yes, upcycled.
ASK: Can a team of Grade 5s sew a pocket from old jeans?
10 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
ASK: Who would want one?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: kids with bag hooks
trap: skipping Can they make it work? for a dream idea.
Fix: ask what it would be built from this term, student re-checks.
notes.stretch: Which check would you weigh most, and why?
notes.help: Point to each picture and say the check with the student.
notes.prep: The model for SC2. These four checks are on the Shark Scorecard and Shark Notes, worded the same way every time.

slides.title: Invest or pass?
slides.pivot: run the four checks aloud together, then re-ask
slides.followUp: cold call one board: which check decided it?

items.answer: Pass - the team can't make it fly

items.answer: Invest - it passes all four checks

say: Shark training. Write invest or pass,
and the check that decided it.
trap: investing in an idea because it sounds fun.
Fix: run all four checks, student names the one it fails.
notes.stretch: Turn one pass into an invest by changing one thing.
notes.help: Give the student the four checks on a card to tick.
notes.prep: First decision point: applying the four checks to new ideas. Grade 6s answer first on their boards. SC2. Eight items, about 8 minutes.

slides.title: What did the shark do?
slides.prompt: A shark puts 3 tokens on Pocket Pal. Point to A, B or C.

options.text: Bought three Pocket Pals to take home
options.misconception: thinks investing means buying the product

options.text: Invested in the Pocket Pal business
Paid the team to make one just for them
options.misconception: thinks investing is ordering a product

beats: SAY: This one matters for Shark Tank Day. Think about the tokens.
ASK: What did the shark do with the tokens?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: B
SCAN Grade 6 fingers first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call a Grade 6: why not A?
Less -> back to the buying and investing table, re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers are scanned.
SAY: B. Tokens help a business grow. Nobody takes a product home. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing A because shops work that way.
Fix: ask what the shark takes home, student says nothing, a share.
notes.prep: Second decision point, aimed at the Grade 6s. Under 80% of Grade 6s means re-teach invest before they meet their teams.

slides.title: Team up and shortlist
slides.task: Grade 5s: meet your business team. Choose three ideas and run the shark checks on each. Grade 6s: be the consultant shark for your team.
slides.frame: Our idea is ___. It fixes ___, and it passes ___ checks.
slides.visualLabel: Team up. Check it. Shortlist it.
slides.extendedTask: a team shortlist of three ideas, each run through the four shark checks

notes.answer: three ideas per team, each with a problem and a checks score
beats: SAY: Read the task, complete each part, then check your work.
Finished early? The Extension. Everyone, together, on three: Team up. Check it. Shortlist it.
SAY: Grade 5s, your team is on the board. Grade 6s, find your team.
Ask your four questions. Don't build for them.
TIME 30 minutes: teams form 5, ideas 10, checks 10, shortlist 5.
CIRCULATE. Ask: which check is your weakest idea failing?
TIME at 30: each team reads out its favourite idea in one sentence.
trap: a team keeping an idea that fails Can they make it work?
Fix: consultant asks what they'd build it from, team swaps the idea.
notes.stretch: Extension: work out the shark's share of a business's earnings.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture clues, checks as yes or no circles.
notes.prep: Teams are set by the teacher from the Session 1 sheets: grouped by shared ideas, not friendships. Keep the shortlists for next week.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A team pitches fridge magnets made from old bottle tops, because notes fall off the fridge.
Invest or pass? Name the check that decided it for you.

notes.answer: invest: real problem, upcycled, makeable, people want it
beats: SAY: A brand new pitch. Judge it on your own, like a real shark.
ASK: Invest or pass? Name the check that decided it.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: invest, it passes all four checks
RECORD who writes invest or pass with no check named.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new pitch. One board per student, Grade 6s included.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the four shark checks from memory.
slides.selfAssessment: Fist to five: how well can you judge an idea like a shark?

notes.answer: Real problem? Upcycled? Can they make it work? Will people want it?
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: Fist to five: how well can you judge an idea like a shark?
5 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mostly three to five
RECORD the fists and ones beside the exit boards.
ASK: Tell your partner the four shark checks.
30 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: problem, upcycled, make it, people want it
